MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JANUARY 29, 2019

A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC) of the City of Rolling Hills
Estates was called to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, by CHAIR SCHMITZ.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Schmitz, Zuckerman, Medawar, Addleman,
  Arata, Bayer, Buresh, Carrese, Friedman, * Seamans,
  Silvano, Stegura

  Committee Members Absent:  Carman, Corman, Portugal, Shinn

  Student Members Present:  Michael Wagreich

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Assistant City Manager
  Grammer, Sr. Planner Naughton, Associate Planner
  Thom, Administrative Assistant Corea
  Also present from Dyett & Bhatia:  Rajeev Bhatia, Principal
  Meghan McNulty, Planner

  * arrived at 6:35 p.m.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  Approval of General Plan Advisory Committee meeting minutes, September 20, 2018.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN MADE A MOTION, SECONDED BY COMMITTEE
  MEMBER MEDAWAR TO,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE GPAC MEETING OF SEPTEMBER 20, 2018
  AS PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Chair Schmitz, Zuckerman, Medawar, Arata, Bayer, Carrese, Friedman,
  Silvano
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Seamans
  ABSTAIN:  Stegura, Buresh, Addleman

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  AGENDA/APPROACH REVIEW

  -  Progress to date
  -  Approach to next set of GPAC meetings

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia, provided a summary on the progress to date and explained
  how the GPAC meetings will be structured going forward.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ requested any questions or comments from the committee on the draft
  Vision and Guiding Principles document.

  After a brief discussion, the following comments/changes were made:
  • Guiding Principles #2 - …The General Plan promotes development patterns and
  enhancements to the circulation network that encourage walking, bicycling,
  equestrian, and transit use explore use of transit in order to minimize traffic
  congestion and reduce greenhouse gas emissions…

  •  Vision Statement – a future discussion is pending on the word “living” since, as it
  currently reads, it implies that residential development in the commercial district has
  the same level of priority as shopping, outdoor dining, and entertainment.

  1
GPAC Meeting Minutes
January 29, 2019
   •  Vision Statement - …Rolling Hills Estates is a model for sustainable practices,
  and is admired for its local environmental resources and natural setting and
  recreational amenities, including trails, parks, and open spaces…

  B.  LAND USE AND COMMUNITY DESIGN ELEMENT WORKBOOK #1
  - Goals

  The committee reviewed and discussed each of the goals in Workbook #1 and agreed on
  the following changes:

  •  Goal 1: No changes - Ensure that future development is compatible with the
  scale and low-density character of existing neighborhoods, is sensitive to the
  local environment and natural settings, and ensure that built-out rural
  neighborhoods remain rural in character.

  •  Goal 2: Ensure that development in residential neighborhoods is limited
  remain consistent with existing development patterns. , while welcoming
  Welcome new residents and businesses development in a vital core in the
  Silver Spur Road commercial district, in appropriately-designed and context-
  sensitive compatible developments.

  •  Goal 3: Promote a socially, vibrant, active, mixed-use district along Silver Spur
  Road the commercial district with uses that include neighborhood- and
  region-serving retail, housing, offices, educational facilities, cultural, dining,
  hotels, and other compatible uses that serve as a destination for residents and
  visitors from the Palos Verdes Peninsula.

  •  Goal 4: The committee agreed to delete this goal due to its similarity to Goal 3.

  •  Goal 5 Goal 4: Ensure that development in the mixed-use commercial district
  is well-designed, fosters an engaging public realm, and promotes Deep Valley
  Drive as a walkable, pedestrian-oriented spine walkability.

  •  Goal 6 Goal 5: Ensure that the use and conversion of the former Palos Verdes
  Landfill remains as undeveloped open space in order protects to protect
  public health and safety of area residents.

  •  Goal 7 Goal 6: No changes - Maintain a balance of land uses and ensure that
  future public uses and needs are adequately considered before allowing reuse,
  or expansion, of institutional sites or land owned by other public agencies.

  •  Goal 7: Maintain park land, trails and open space to serve the equestrian,
  recreational, and social needs of the community and provide the
  necessary public services and infrastructure.

  -  Key decisions regarding commercial districts

  Mr. Bhatia explained that there is a basic land use designation and then there are a series
  of overlays. He further explained the mixed-use overlay and requested that the committee
  hold a discussion on whether or not to limit housing in the mixed-use overlay area.

  A discussion ensued on the amount of mixed-use. The Committee agreed that residential
  should be limited to certain areas of the commercial district. Key points of discussion were
  as follows:

  •  Town & Country to remain commercial only
  •  Limit mixed-use on Deep Valley Drive
  •  Limit mixed-use on Silver Spur Road
  •  Limit mixed-use on Bart Earle Way

  Further discussion ensued regarding how much residential development to allow on the
  south side of Deep Valley Drive. It was determined that it should be limited from the Library
  to Town and Country (Roxcove Drive). The committee also discussed conserving space
  for offices in the commercial district, and a need for gathering space or a central park in the
  middle of the Promenade site.

 6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS (Verbal Reports)

  NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Mr. Bhatia stated that for the next meeting, some of the items to be discussed will be, the
  Promenade site, open space, and the remaining overlays. There may be an interactive
  exercise where committee members will highlight characteristics, qualities, open spaces,
  and features they like in the neighborhoods throughout the city.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:48 p.m.
